{{Short description|Disproven conjecture for a primality test}}
In [[number theory]], the '''Chinese hypothesis''' is a disproven [[conjecture]] stating that an [[integer]] ''n'' is [[Prime number|prime]] [[if and only if]] it satisfies the condition that <math>2^n-2</math> is [[divisible]] by ''n''—in other words, that an integer ''n'' is prime if and only if <math>2^n \equiv 2 \bmod{n}</math>. It is true that if ''n'' is prime, then <math>2^n \equiv 2 \bmod{n}</math> (this is a special case of [[Fermat's little theorem]]), however the [[converse (logic)|converse]] (if <math>2^n \equiv 2 \bmod{n}</math> then ''n'' is prime) is false, and therefore the hypothesis as a whole is false. The smallest [[counterexample]] is ''n'' = 341 = 11×31. [[Composite number]]s ''n'' for which <math>2^n-2</math> is divisible by ''n'' are called [[Poulet number]]s. They are a special class of [[Fermat pseudoprime]]s.

==History==
Once, and sometimes still, mistakenly thought to be of ancient Chinese origin, the Chinese hypothesis actually originates in the mid-19th century from the work of [[Qing dynasty]] mathematician [[Li Shanlan]] (1811–1882).<ref name=Ribenboim2006>{{cite book |last=Ribenboim |first=Paulo |author-link=Paulo Ribenboim |year=2006 |title=The Little Book of Bigger Primes |publisher=Springer Science & Business Media |isbn=9780387218205 |pages=88–89}}</ref> He was later made aware his statement was incorrect and removed it from his subsequent work but it was not enough to prevent the false proposition from appearing elsewhere under his name;<ref name=Ribenboim2006/> a later mistranslation in the 1898 work of Jeans dated the conjecture to Confucian times and gave birth to the ancient origin myth.<ref name=Ribenboim2006/><ref>{{cite book |last=Needham |first=Joseph |author-link=Joseph Needham |others=In collaboration with Wang Ling |year=1959 |title=Science and Civilisation in China |volume=3: Mathematics and the Sciences of the Heavens and the Earth |publisher=Cambridge University Press |location=Cambridge, England |page=54}} (all of footnote d)</ref>
